biological.citation: Roles and mechanisms of ankyrin-G in neuropsychiatric disorders (PMID: 35794211)
biological.summary: ANK3 encodes ankyrin-G, a molecular scaffold that plays an essential role in localizing proteins to the axon initial segment (AIS) and nodes of Ranvier, as well as to the dendritic shaft and spines in neurons. Ankyrin-G isoforms vary in expression according to the stage of brain development and have distinct functional differences. Posttranslational modifications of ankyrin-G affect its protein expression, interactions, and subcellular localization, with implications for bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and ASD pathogenesis.

biological.citation: Lithium restores inhibitory function and neuronal excitability through GSK-3β inhibition in a bipolar disorder-associated Ank3 variant mouse model (PMID: 40849089)
biological.summary: The BD-associated ANK3 variant p.W1989R disrupts the ankyrin-G/GABARAP interaction, resulting in inhibitory deficits and cortical pyramidal neuron hyperexcitability in mice. Chronic lithium treatment selectively enhances presynaptic GABAergic neurotransmission, reduces neuronal hyperexcitability, and partially rescues AIS length in this mouse model. The GSK-3β inhibitor Tideglusib recapitulates the enhancement of presynaptic GABAergic signaling, implicating GSK-3β inhibition as the mechanism.

biological.citation: Impaired OTUD7A-dependent Ankyrin regulation mediates neuronal dysfunction in mouse and human models of the 15q13.3 microdeletion syndrome (PMID: 36604605)
biological.summary: OTUD7A interacts with Ankyrin-G (Ank3) and Ankyrin-B (Ank2) in neurons, and this interaction is disrupted by an epilepsy-associated OTUD7A L233F variant. In 15q13.3 microdeletion and OTUD7AL233F/L233F mouse and human iPSC-derived neuron models, Ankyrin-G shows protein instability, increased polyubiquitination, and decreased levels at the axon initial segment, with reduced Ankyrin-G nanodomains in dendritic spines. Restoring OTUD7A or Ankyrin-G expression in 15q13.3 microdeletion neurons reversed abnormalities in axonal growth and intrinsic excitability.

biological.citation: Mood, stress and longevity: convergence on ANK3 (PMID: 27217151)
biological.summary: C. elegans inactivating mutants for ANK3/unc-44 survive longer than wild-type worms, particularly in older animals, independently of mianserin treatment. Wild-type ANK3/unc-44 expression increases with age in C. elegans and is maintained at lower levels by the antidepressant mianserin, with lower levels associated with improved longevity. Some ANK3/unc-44 expression is necessary for mianserin's effects on prolonging lifespan and survival under oxidative stress, particularly in younger worms, suggesting antagonistic pleiotropy.

biological.citation: Mapping the expression of an ANK3 isoform associated with bipolar disorder in the human brain (PMID: 35091539)
biological.summary: A BD-associated ANK3 isoform shows significantly higher expression in the corpus callosum compared to frontal tissue in postmortem brain samples. In a child-development cohort, adolescents expressed this isoform at clearly higher levels than younger children, suggesting a role in myelin maturation of the human brain. A loss-of-function variant (rs41283526*G) in the alternatively spliced exon has a protective effect against BD, implying elevated expression of this isoform is a risk factor.
biological.significance: p < 1e-4 (corpus callosum vs frontal); p = 5e-3 (adolescents vs younger children)

biological.citation: Identification of 4 novel human ocular coloboma genes ANK3, BMPR1B, PDGFRA, and CDH4 through evolutionary conserved vertebrate gene analysis (PMID: 35034853)
biological.summary: Zebrafish ank3a expression was localized to the optic fissure and surrounding regions during early eye development. Knockdown of ank3 in zebrafish revealed a coloboma and/or microphthalmia phenotype, and novel pathogenic ANK3 variants were identified in unrelated coloboma families from the 100,000 Genomes Project. These findings establish ANK3 as a novel causative gene for ocular coloboma through cross-species comparative meta-analysis.

biological.citation: Expression of ANK3 moderates the association between childhood trauma and affective traits in severe mental disorders (PMID: 37620394)
biological.summary: ANK3 mRNA levels in whole blood were measured in 174 patients with bipolar disorder and 291 patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder. Patients with both high ANK3 expression and the most severe childhood sexual abuse had more manic/hypomanic episodes and an earlier age at onset. ANK3 expression levels moderated the relationship between emotional neglect and manic/hypomanic episodes, suggesting ANK3 acts as a biological moderator between early trauma and affective outcomes.

biological.citation: Loss of ANK3 Function Causes a Recessive Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Cerebellar Ataxia (PMID: 40879451)
biological.summary: Five individuals from three unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous ANK3 predicted loss-of-function variants presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, variable epilepsy, and cerebellar signs including ataxia, tremor, and dysarthria. Cerebellar atrophy predominantly affecting the superior vermis and cerebellar hemispheres was observed on MRI. These clinical findings align with murine models lacking the cerebellar ankyrin-G isoform, which exhibit ataxic features and high cerebellar ANK3 expression.

ANK3 is identified as a small regulatory protein involved in renal magnesium handling, specifically in the context of intrarenal channels and transporters related to Mg2+ absorption. Unraveling rare genetic diseases with dysmagnesemia has implicated ANK3 alongside tight junction proteins, apical ion channels, and basolateral proteins in the complex regulatory network of kidney Mg2+ homeostasis. This places ANK3 in the pathway of renal magnesium reabsorption.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Genetic variation in the AnkyrinG interactome causes a range of neurological disorders (F. Kooy et al.)
biological.summary: The AnkyrinG protein-protein interaction (PPI) network includes 17 direct interactors: cell adhesion molecules, cytoskeleton-component β4-spectrin, specific sodium and potassium channel components, and components of Casein kinase 2. MIP sequencing of all genes in the ANK3 PPI network in over 1009 patient-parent trios identified 14 confirmed de novo variants in multiple ANK3 PPI network members, a significant overrepresentation compared to expectation. This demonstrates that the AnkyrinG PPI network as a whole is under selective pressure and relevant to neurodevelopmental disorders.
